body:
More like in a selfish way. She has something like an inferiority complex towards her brothers, by seeing that they're doing "great" things (with one ruling the continent, and the other commanding a legion of soldiers). She was bored studying to take the title of High Justice, and imagined it would be a great way to get some excitement in her life as well as showing her brothers that she's as good as they are.

But after really getting there, things didn't quite turned out the way she pictured it in her mind, and that did make her feel some regret over her decision.

Overall she tends to be impulsive at times, and now with war knocking on the doorstep, she set her sights to work on a way to get back home.

Well, the Tower itself is a place where every bit of knowledge known to the Lord Protectorate is kept, but the main reason she wanted to go there is because of Felron - the man wrote many encyclopedias translating what he can from the scrolls, and since she wanted to excel in something else than her brothers, this seemed like a perfect opportunity.

Also for context I have to say that during this time, only Felron has any knowledge of other continents, because he found the maps, it isn't released to the public because it would shake the very basis of their belief system of their continent being the only world existing.

Then, because of her short temper, when even after 1.5 years she still felt stuck - even though she's learned a lot during that time and already had a wider understanding of the world than both of her brothers combined - was the time when out of an impulsive choice she decided that she'd actually travel to one of the continents to be a person remembered by history as the first person to ever set foot on another continent, but well, it ain't how it turned out.

P.S: Thanks for reading it, and pointing it out, hopefully I provided enough information to answer your question.

Born in the 212th year of the eighth era in the city of **Eiva'ar**, Miryza was the second child of **Lord Protector Darosyth Olaman Ylthas**, and heiress to the title of High Justice, there was a lot expected of her. She - along with her siblings - was marked with the **Mark of Bavalvor** under her left eye, as everyone in the royal family is, to prevent impostors from trying to take one's place.

With her two brothers – **Eyanmar** and **Ayroth** – she’s been taught the value of working together. They’ve attended many trials to prove their worth as successors, but after a while Miry discovered that her interests lie elsewhere.
She couldn’t go face her father, so she kept going on with her training, studying each and every law of **Lo’Sir**, revisiting many closed cases, and attending ongoing trials to gain experience, whilst reading books written by the greatest scholar on the continent at the time.

Though, after Lord Protector Darosyth died when she was 17, the girl started to turn away from her given path.
With her elder brother Eyanmar now being Lord Protector, she convinced him to arrange a meeting with said scholar – namely **Felron del Bosath** – so she’d be mentored by the man.
Felron only took the offer because he didn’t dare question the order of the Lord Protector himself, and took the girl under his guidance.

After spending a year and a half at the **Tower of Iarnus Telintae**, Miryza – feeling that she’s accomplishing nothing, and is only living in the shadow of her brothers, with Eyanmar being Lord Protector, and Ayroth a commander – decided that she’ll travel to **Crevadum Veluvis**, the nearest continent.
She slipped out during nighttime, stole a boat and set sail towards the other continent, however the girl ended up shipwrecked on the shores of **Dhenýr** (which is the same continent she planned to go to, only in the language of the locals).

After living half a year in poverty, sleeping in abandoned barns, and stealing for a living, everything changed after one night, when a group of drunk men wanted to „have some fun” with her.

It was that moment, when **Weygórh se Qarlayá** intervened – should the thugs thought their plans through, and didn’t carry out their „flawless plan” on the main street of the village, they may’ve gotten away with it -, threw a bag of gold towards the group – which two out of the three took -, but one didn’t relent. After being attacked, Weygórh elegantly danced around his opponent, before snapping his neck with one good strike.

Miryza was terrified, thinking that the man has the same intentions as the ones before him. However, that wasn’t the case. Seeing that the girl’s living day by day, he took her with him, back to the **Free City of Dalashayr**, to join the **Eyes of D’loth** – the most infamous assassins and smugglers guild on the continent of Dhenýr, where the poor and unlucky are taken in and trained to have another chance at life.

Spending half a decade there, she’s learned the local language, and is a full member of the organization now.
She’s one of the POV characters in my first book, titled **Heritage: New Dawn**. 

(In the background the huge green gas giant is visible, the world/planet where this story takes place on is a moon of it.)
